text:
alex: seeing a reproducible perf regression when continuous batching is enabled + large long-context requests (20k tokens). memory for KV store keeps growing and we hit head-of-line delays. repro minimal: run local loadgen with mixed seq-lens + cont-batch on

sam: ugh. roughly when did this start? after kernels change last week?

alex: yes noticed after the kernel-selector tweak that picks tiled-attn for a subset of layers. suspect fragmentation: we are allocating KV pages for different kernel paths and not reusing slots across batch merges/splits. attaching profiler snippet below.

maria: can you paste the perf flame or pprof? small snippets are easiest to scan. :mag_right:

alex: pasted, here's a trimmed stack and a short log excerpt:
```
Flame: runtime::kv::alloc_slot -> kv_pager::evict_if_needed -> continuous_batch::merge_batches -> kv_slot_reuse_miss
CPU samples show spikes in memcpy and page_table_walk.
```
Logs:
```
[2026-03-10T14:23:12Z] batch-id=342 merge:start size_pre=6 size_post=2
[2026-03-10T14:23:12Z] kv:alloc page=0x7f3a size=64k owner=batch-342
[2026-03-10T14:23:12Z] evict:start threshold=0.85 used=0.88
[2026-03-10T14:23:12Z] evict:removed pages=4 (fragmented)
[2026-03-10T14:23:12Z] kv:alloc page=0x7f3b size=64k owner=batch-343
```

jun: this smells like split/merge churn: when merge reduces batch count we should try to reuse pages from the merged batches but we may be racing with eviction and kernel path changes leading to different page layouts.

olivia: in our code there is an invariant that pages are bound to kernel-paths to simplify kernel-local memory layout. that makes reuse harder if kernel selector flips. maybe we should relax binding for KV pages?

sam: relaxing binding could improve reuse but might hurt specialized kernels that depend on packed layout. tradeoff. what if we add a short grace window: on merge, mark pages as "quarantine" for X ms so a following split can reuse without reallocation?

maria: we tried a quarantine window in q4 for LRU churn, it helped for small contexts but not for long-context streams where merges/splits are frequent and ordering causes head-of-line blocking. Do we have measurements for HOL blocking vs eviction overhead?

alex: yes, quick numbers from the loadgen run (all with cont-batch enabled):
- baseline (no cont-batch): p95 latency 230ms, kv-allocs/sec ~120, mem-stable
- cont-batch v1 (current): p95 340ms, kv-allocs/sec ~420, mem grows +25% over 30m
- cont-batch + quarantine(50ms): p95 300ms, kv-allocs/sec ~260, but HOL stalls still observed during bursts

grace: maybe the issue is ordering: a large long-context request at head of queue holds a hot KV slot that prevents merged batches behind it from progressing — head-of-line blocking. If continuous batching merges smaller requests behind the long request into the same batch, KV page ownership toggles and we create fragmentation. Could we change merge policy to avoid merging across requests with >N tokens outstanding?

jun: that could be a low-risk change: treat requests with sequence_length > threshold as "no-merge" candidates. threshold could be percentile-based (eg 95th) to avoid hurting throughput.

olivia: implementing that is straightforward: in batcher when scoring merge candidates, add check: if (req.max_leftover_tokens > LONG_CTX_THRESH) skip merging. Also need to ensure fallback uses a compatible kernel profile to avoid cross-path allocs.

alex: I can prototype a patch. also want to try pinning kernel selection for merged batches to the kernel of the first request to avoid kernel-path churn. That should reduce layout variance.

sam: yes pinning seems promising: when merge happens, compute chosen_kernel = policy(first_request, merged_size) and enforce for batch lifetime. downside: may not be globally optimal but better than oscillation.

maria: for immediate triage can we run 3 experiments on staging:
1) disable cont-batch (control)
2) cont-batch + no-merge-for-long-ctx
3) cont-batch + pin-kernel-on-merge
Collect metrics: p95 latency, kv-allocs/sec, mem-growth 30m, eviction_count, HOL-block incidents (we have a metric count_hol_block).

alex: doing that now. starting experiment 2 first. will run 1h each.

ci-bot: deploy request queued: alex/contbatch-no-merge -> staging (run-1). CI checks passed: unit tests + basic perf smoke. :white_check_mark:

alex: experiment 2 results (30m): p95 265ms, kv-allocs/sec 210, mem-growth 8% over 30m, eviction_count down 45%, hol_block events down but not eliminated.

sam: promising. experiment 3 next?

alex: experiment 3 (pin-kernel) running...

olivia: one more thought: the KV pager uses 64k page slab. fragmentation grows because merged batches create lots of small live regions inside pages. Could we try smaller slab (16k) for kernel-agnostic pages to reduce internal fragmentation? Might increase metadata overhead though.

jun: worth testing but do as A/B not to regress other workloads.

alex: pin-kernel results (30m): p95 280ms, kv-allocs/sec 190, mem-growth 3% over 30m, eviction_count down 60%, hol_block nearly gone. CPU overhead slightly up (~3%).

maria: so pinning wins on HOL and memory. quarantine helped partially. Action items:
- alex: open PR for merge policy change + kernel pinning prototype (include flags)
- olivia: experiment with mixed slab sizes for kernel-bound vs kernel-agnostic pages
- jun: add metric for "kernel-path-churn" (count kernel switches per batch id)
- sam: schedule canary on dedicated cluster next week

alex: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/1428 (WIP)

grace: nice. let's keep short feature flag TTLs and roll slowly. also add a regression test that simulates long-context + frequent splits/merges to catch this in CI.

alex: agreed, adding test to perf-harness. thanks all :pray:

sam: great detective work everyone. we'll regroup after canary. :thumbsup:
